issue.title: Move the artifact-file index into sase-core's Rust indexed storage
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-l6.6 (land phase of epic sase-l6, SASE CONTEXT incremental enrichment); named as follow-up 2 in plans:202608/sase_context_incremental.md.

The artifact-file index (~/.sase/artifacts/index.jsonl, 7.68 MB / 7,747 rows as of 2026-08-13, larger now) is a single JSONL file re-parsed by every process that reads it (src/sase/core/artifact_file_explicit.py:read_artifact_file_index). Epic sase-l6 phase sase-l6.2 added a process-wide revalidating snapshot cache on top of it (one parse per process per store change), which was deliberately scoped as a caching fix, not a storage-format change — the plan explicitly called moving the index into Rust core's indexed storage 'a schema decision' out of scope for that phase.

Scope: evaluate migrating this index into sase-core's indexed storage (crates/sase_core), following the Rust-core-backend-boundary convention already used for the agent-artifact-index sqlite DB (see sase-kh), so parsing cost and memory footprint stop scaling with every reading process across the fleet, not just within one process's cache lifetime. Take epic sase-l6's measurements (per-lane resolver cost tables in the sase-l6.1/sase-l6.6 close notes and docs/perf_runbook.md) as the sizing input. Work in sase-core through /sase_repo (sase repo open sase-core) and read that repo's AGENTS.md first.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-lr — this epic's store-pruning follow-up for the same three JSONL stores; a retention policy and a storage-format migration are complementary, not competing, and should be sequenced by whoever picks either up. RELATED: sase-kh — prior art for moving a similarly-shaped per-process-reparsed store (the agent-artifact-index sqlite DB) into sase-core, useful as a template for scope and API shape.
